original_sentence: Some might say that we work because we have to, not least because we need the salary that enables us to be financially independent.
definitionEn: a fixed amount of money paid regularly for professional or office work

posExamples.sentence: The research institute offers graduates a competitive salary.
Her salary is deposited on the final working day of each month.
The board froze senior salaries during the downturn.

wordForms.noun: salary 薪金（复数 salaries）
wordForms.adjective: salaried 拿薪水的、受薪的（a salaried employee 领薪雇员）
wordForms.other: 重音在第一音节 /ˈsæləri/；复数变 y→ies：salaries；词源为拉丁语 salarium“盐钱”（古罗马发给士兵买盐的津贴）

collocations.phrase: need the salary that enables us to be financially independent
collocations.translation: 课文原句：需要使我们经济独立的薪水
collocations.example: Some might say that we work because we have to, not least because we need the salary that enables us to be financially independent. 有人可能会说，我们工作是因为不得不工作，尤其是因为我们需要能使我们经济独立的薪水。
She earns a good salary as an engineer. 她当工程师，薪水不错。
His annual salary is 300,000 yuan. 他的年薪是三十万元。
She asked for a salary increase. 她要求加薪。
He is on a salary of $40,000 a year. 他年薪四万美元。
How can they justify paying such huge salaries? 他们怎能为支付如此高的薪水辩解？
The vacancy offers a competitive salary package and medical insurance.
The government refused to freeze public-sector salaries during the crisis.

synonyms.example: The workers are paid low wages. 工人们的工资很低。
synonyms.usage: salary 指按月／年支付给职员、专业人员的固定薪金，搭配 annual/monthly salary、on a salary of；wage(s) 指按小时、日或周付给体力劳动者的工钱，常用复数；pay 是两者的统称。

synonyms.example: He has a monthly income of 8,000 yuan. 他月收入八千元。
synonyms.usage: income 范围最广，指工资、利息、租金等一切收入来源；salary 只指工作所得薪金。income 常与 high/low、annual、source of 搭配。

synonyms.example: His earnings have doubled in two years. 他的收入两年翻了一番。
synonyms.usage: earnings 为复数形式名词，指靠劳动挣得的钱的总和；salary 是其中按月发放的固定部分。

advancedExpressions.expression: 课文原句 Some might say that we work because we have to, not least because we need the salary that enables us to be financially independent. 中 that 引导宾语从句作 say 的宾语；that 在从句中不作成分、无词义，但从句内部另含原因状语从句时一般不省略 that
advancedExpressions.example: Some might say (that) we work because we have to. 有人可能会说，我们工作是因为不得不工作。

advancedExpressions.expression: salary（月薪/年薪）/ wage（时薪/周薪）/ pay（统称）/ income（一切收入）/ earnings（劳动所得）/ fee（服务费）/ pension（退休金）
advancedExpressions.example: His income includes a salary and various fees. 他的收入包括薪金和各种服务费。

advancedExpressions.expression: be financially independent 经济独立 / financial independence 财务独立 / support oneself 养活自己 / live within one's means 量入为出
advancedExpressions.example: The salary enables us to be financially independent. 这份薪水使我们能够经济独立。

translation: n. & vi. n. 劳工；劳动，（尤指）体力劳动；分娩期，分娩 vi. 努力做；干苦力活（美式拼写 labor）
original_sentence: It is certainly true that most of us do join the labour force once our studies are completed.
definitionEn: (1) work, especially hard physical work (2) workers as a group (3) the process of childbirth (4) to work very hard

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 劳动，（尤指）体力劳动；（总称）人工，劳动力
uncommonMeanings.example: The price will include the labour and materials. 价格将包括人工费和材料费。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 一段时间的辛苦工作，辛劳（the day's labours）
uncommonMeanings.example: He was so exhausted from the day's labours that he went straight to bed. 他因一天的劳累精疲力竭，径直上床睡了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 分娩，临产（be in labour / go into labour）
uncommonMeanings.example: Jane was in labour for ten hours. 简分娩了十个小时。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 努力做（labour to do sth / labour over sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: They laboured to finish the job on time. 他们努力按时完成工作。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 干苦力活，辛苦劳作
uncommonMeanings.example: We laboured from dawn to dusk in the fields. 我们在田里从早到晚劳作。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （大写 Labour）英国工党
uncommonMeanings.example: He has always voted Labour. 他一直投工党的票。

posExamples.sentence: Volunteers supplied the labour needed to rebuild the footbridge.
Mechanics laboured through the night to restore the damaged engine.
The patient went into labour shortly after midnight.

wordForms.noun: labour 劳动；劳工；分娩；labourer 体力劳动者，劳工
wordForms.adjective: laborious 费力的，辛苦的；labouring 劳动的（the labouring classes 劳动阶级）
wordForms.other: 美式拼写 labor；重音在第一音节 /ˈleɪbə(r)/；作“劳动／劳动力”不可数，复数 labours 指“一段时间的辛劳”

idioms.example: Restoring the old house was a labour of love. 修复这座老屋是心甘情愿的辛劳。

collocations.translation: 课文原句：加入劳动力大军
collocations.example: Most of us do join the labour force once our studies are completed. 我们大多数人的确在完成学业后就加入劳动力大军。
He earns his living by manual labour. 他靠体力劳动谋生。
The company wants to keep down labour costs. 公司想压低劳动力成本。

collocations.translation: 【课件】廉价／熟练劳动力的短缺
collocations.example: There is a shortage of skilled labour in the region. 该地区熟练劳动力短缺。
Jane was in labour for ten hours. 简分娩了十个小时。
He's been labouring over the report since Wednesday. 自星期三以来他一直忙着写这份报告。
They laboured for years to clear their son's name. 他们多年来努力为儿子洗清罪名。
We laboured from dawn to dusk in the fields. 我们在田里从早到晚劳作。

collocations.translation: 【课件】劳动阶级（= the working class）
collocations.example: The labouring classes had little access to education then. 那时劳动阶级几乎没有受教育的机会。

synonyms.example: She's looking for work in publishing. 她在出版业找工作。
synonyms.usage: work 最普通，泛指一切脑力或体力工作；labour 较正式，强调辛苦的体力劳动，不可数，多与 manual、costs、skilled 搭配。

synonyms.example: They toiled in the fields all day. 他们在田里辛苦劳作了一整天。
synonyms.usage: toil 为书面语，名词/不及物动词，强调长时间艰苦劳作（toil away at sth）；labour 兼有“劳动力”“分娩”等义，义项更多。

advancedExpressions.expression: manual labour 体力劳动 / labour costs 劳动力成本 / skilled labour 熟练劳动力 / be in labour 分娩 / labour over sth 埋头做 / labour to do sth 努力做 / labour from dawn to dusk 起早贪黑地干 / the labouring classes 劳动阶级
advancedExpressions.example: He's been labouring over the report since Wednesday. 自星期三以来他一直埋头写这份报告。

advancedExpressions.expression: 课文原句 It is certainly true that most of us do join the labour force… 为 It 作形式主语、that 从句作真正主语的主语从句：It is + adj. + that 从句；once our studies are completed 是时间状语从句
advancedExpressions.example: It is certainly true that most of us join the labour force after graduation. 我们大多数人毕业后加入劳动力大军，这一点千真万确。

advancedExpressions.expression: labour → labourer（-er 表“……的人”）→ laborious（-ious 形容词后缀，费力的）→ labouring（现在分词作定语）
advancedExpressions.example: Weeding the garden is a laborious task. 给园子除草是件费力的活。

classPractice.note: labour over sth 埋头苦干于；since 提示现在完成进行时 has been labouring。

original_sentence: It is certainly true that most of us do join the labour force once our studies are completed.
definitionEn: all the people in a country or area who are available for work

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （一国、一地区或一企业的）全体劳动力，劳动人口（集合名词，常用单数）
uncommonMeanings.example: The country's labour force is shrinking. 该国劳动力正在萎缩。

posExamples.sentence: More women entered the labour force after childcare services expanded.
Automation is changing the skills required across the labour force.
The region's ageing labour force worries local manufacturers.

wordForms.noun: labour force = workforce 劳动力；labour market 劳动力市场；labourer 劳工
wordForms.other: 集合名词，作主语时谓语一般用单数；美式拼写 labor force

collocations.phrase: join the labour force once our studies are completed
collocations.translation: 课文原句：一完成学业就加入劳动力大军
collocations.example: Most of us do join the labour force once our studies are completed. 我们大多数人的确在完成学业后就加入劳动力大军。

collocations.translation: 【课件】廉价／熟练劳动力的短缺
collocations.example: The industry faces a shortage of skilled labour. 该行业面临熟练劳动力短缺。
Millions of graduates enter the labour force every year. 每年有数百万毕业生进入劳动力市场。

collocations.translation: 老龄化的／不断萎缩的劳动力
collocations.example: Japan faces an ageing labour force. 日本面临劳动力老龄化。
More women have joined the labour force in recent decades. 近几十年来更多女性加入了劳动力大军。
The technology sector depends on a highly skilled labour force.
Affordable childcare could expand the labour force significantly.
Labour-force participation rose among workers over fifty.

synonyms.example: Half of the workforce is on strike. 半数员工在罢工。
synonyms.usage: workforce 与 labour force 基本同义可互换；workforce 更常指一家公司的全体员工，labour force 更常指一国/一地区的劳动人口。均为集合名词，谓语常用单数。

synonyms.example: The school has a staff of forty. 这所学校有四十名教职工。
synonyms.usage: staff 指某一单位的全体职员（多为脑力工作者）；labour force 指宏观意义上的劳动人口。英式英语中 staff 谓语可用复数。

advancedExpressions.expression: labour force = workforce；labour market 劳动力市场；working population 劳动人口；human resources 人力资源
advancedExpressions.example: Women now make up nearly half of the labour force. 如今女性占劳动力的近一半。

advancedExpressions.expression: 课文原句 It is certainly true that most of us do join the labour force… ：It 为形式主语，that 引导的主语从句是真正主语（本单元语法：名词性从句综述）；do join 中 do 表强调
advancedExpressions.example: It is true that many graduates join the labour force immediately after college. 许多毕业生大学一毕业就加入劳动力大军，这是事实。

advancedExpressions.expression: join the labour force once our studies are completed（课文原句：一完成学业就加入劳动力大军） / a shortage of cheap/skilled labour（【课件】廉价／熟练劳动力的短缺） / enter/join the labour force（进入／加入劳动力市场） / an ageing/a shrinking labour force（老龄化的／不断萎缩的劳动力）
advancedExpressions.example: Most of us do join the labour force once our studies are completed. 我们大多数人的确在完成学业后就加入劳动力大军。

translation: vt. & n. vt. 使适合于 n. 排挡，齿轮，传动装置
definitionEn: (1) equipment or clothing used for an activity (2) a toothed wheel or a vehicle mechanism (3) to design or adapt something for a purpose

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 排挡，齿轮，传动装置（first gear 一挡；change gear 换挡）
uncommonMeanings.example: The car has five gears. 这辆车有五个挡。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （某活动的）用具，装备（camping/fishing gear）
uncommonMeanings.example: We packed all our camping gear into the car. 我们把野营用具都装上了车。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （口语）衣服，服装（football gear/sports gear）
uncommonMeanings.example: The kids arrived in their football gear. 孩子们穿着足球服来了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使适合于，使适应（常用被动 be geared to/towards sth）
uncommonMeanings.example: The programme is geared to the needs of beginners. 该课程是为满足初学者的需要而设计的。

posExamples.sentence: Climbers checked their safety gear before leaving camp.
The mechanic shifted into a lower gear on the steep descent.
The literacy programme is geared towards adult learners.

wordForms.noun: gear 齿轮；排挡；装备；gearbox 变速箱
wordForms.verb: gear（使）适合；gear up（使）做好准备
wordForms.other: gear 作“装备／衣服”讲不可数；change gear、in gear 等挡位短语中 gear 前不加冠词；发音 /ɡɪə(r)/

idioms.translation: 进入状态，开始顺利运转
idioms.example: After the break, the team quickly got into gear. 休息之后，团队很快进入了状态。

collocations.translation: 【课件】旨在，为……而设计（be designed to achieve a particular purpose）
collocations.example: The course has been geared towards/to the specific needs of its members. 课程已调整以满足学员的特别需要。
All students are gearing up for the coming examination. 所有的学生正在为即将到来的考试做准备。

collocations.phrase: be geared up for sth / to do sth
collocations.example: We have people on board geared up to help with any problems. 我们船上有已做好准备帮助解决任何问题的人员。
He put the car into gear and drove off. 他挂上挡把车开走了。
Don't forget to bring your sports gear. 别忘了带运动服装。
He carried all his photography gear up the hill. 他背着全套摄影器材上了山。
Change gear before you climb the hill. 上坡前先换挡。
Fire crews checked their protective gear before entering the tunnel.

synonyms.example: The lab has modern equipment. 实验室有现代化设备。
synonyms.usage: equipment 正式、泛指各类设备；gear 口语色彩强，指某项活动的成套用具或服装。两者都不可数。

synonyms.translation: 使适应（对应 be geared to）
synonyms.example: The course was adapted to the students' level. 课程已按学生水平调整。
synonyms.usage: be geared to/towards 多用被动、后接名词，强调“专为……设计”；adapt 主动被动均常用，adapt sth to sth / adapt to sth。

advancedExpressions.expression: be geared to/towards sth 旨在适合 / gear up for sth 为……做准备 / be geared up for sth（to do sth）已做好准备 / put a car into gear 挂挡 / change gear 换挡 / sports gear 运动装备
advancedExpressions.example: All students are gearing up for the coming examination. 所有学生都在为即将到来的考试做准备。

advancedExpressions.expression: gear up for = prepare for = get ready for = make preparations for
advancedExpressions.example: The whole city is gearing up for the games. 全城正在为运动会做准备。

advancedExpressions.expression: be geared towards/to sth（【课件】旨在，为……而设计（be designed to achieve a particular purpose）） / gear up for sth（【课件】为……做准备） / be geared up for sth / to do sth（【课件】为……做好准备） / put a car into gear（【课件】给汽车挂挡）
advancedExpressions.example: The course has been geared towards/to the specific needs of its members. 课程已调整以满足学员的特别需要。

definitionEn: to obtain the money needed for daily life by working

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 挣得，赚得（钱）
uncommonMeanings.example: He earns £30,000 a year. 他一年挣三万英镑。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （因品质、成就）赢得，博得（赞扬、尊重、名声）；earn sb sth 为某人赢得
uncommonMeanings.example: Her honesty earned her the respect of her colleagues. 她的诚实为她赢得了同事的尊重。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （钱）生（利息），带来（收益）
uncommonMeanings.example: Your savings earn interest in the bank. 你的存款在银行生息。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: living 生计（a living 谋生之道；标准搭配 earn/make a living）
uncommonMeanings.example: What does he do for a living? 他靠什么谋生？

posExamples.sentence: Maya earns a living by repairing musical instruments.
Seasonal workers earn a living from the summer harvest.
He moved abroad to earn a living as a chef.

wordForms.noun: earnings（复数形式）薪水，收入；living 生计
wordForms.other: earn sb sth 为双宾语结构：His ability earned him a place；earn one's living 中 living 前常用物主代词；【课件】earnings 薪水、收入

collocations.example: He earns a living as a street musician. 他靠街头演奏谋生。

collocations.phrase: earn a living by doing sth
collocations.example: She earns her living by teaching. 她靠教书谋生。
He took a part-time job to earn money. 他做兼职赚钱。
She worked hard and earned a scholarship. 她努力学习，获得了奖学金。
He earned a fortune in real estate. 他做房地产挣了大钱。
She earned praise for her courage. 她因勇气而赢得赞扬。

original_sentence: In a successful, stable and productive society, all jobs are equally important and no one is superior to another, so we should not have prejudice against any of them.
definitionEn: an unfair and unreasonable opinion or feeling formed without enough knowledge, especially about a group

original_sentence: Whether we are scientists, lawyers, doctors, public servants, consultants, clerks, receptionists or butchers, we all make our respective contributions.
definitionEn: belonging or relating separately to each of two or more people or things already mentioned

posExamples.sentence: The two researchers returned to their respective laboratories.
Players shook hands before taking their respective positions.
The reports describe the respective roles of the two agencies.

wordForms.noun: respect 尊敬；方面（in this respect 在这方面）
wordForms.adjective: respective 各自的；respectable 值得尊敬的，体面的；respectful 恭敬的，有礼貌的；respected 受人尊敬的
wordForms.adverb: respectively 分别地，各自地（常置句末，与前面并列成分一一对应）
wordForms.other: respective 只能作定语（放在复数名词前），不能作表语；不能说 The offices are respective。

collocations.translation: 做出我们各自的贡献（课文原句）
collocations.example: We all make our respective contributions. 我们都做出各自的贡献。
They are experts in their respective fields. 他们是各自领域的专家。

collocations.translation: 各自的……（respective 只作定语，后接复数名词）
collocations.example: After the party, we went back to our respective homes. 聚会后我们回到各自的家。
The managers returned to their respective departments after lunch.
The contract defines the partners' respective responsibilities.
Both agencies explained their respective roles in the rescue.
The lost bags were returned to their respective owners.
After the ceremony, the families went back to their respective homes.

synonyms.example: Each student has a locker. 每个学生都有一个储物柜。
synonyms.usage: each 修饰单数名词、可作主语或代词；respective 只作定语且必须修饰复数名词，强调'与各主体一一对应'：they returned to their respective rooms = each returned to his/her own room。

synonyms.example: They slept in separate rooms. 他们睡在不同的房间。
synonyms.usage: separate 强调'彼此分开、互不相同'，可作定语或表语；respective 强调'各归各的归属关系'，只作定语。

advancedExpressions.expression: respectable 值得尊敬的/体面的（人、职业）→ a respectable job；respectful 恭敬的（态度）→ be respectful to elders；respected 受尊敬的 → a respected scholar；respective 各自的 → their respective duties
advancedExpressions.example: 四个形容词高考常一起考，按'体面—恭敬—受敬—各自'口诀记。

advancedExpressions.expression: A and B are ... respectively 分别是……（句末，与前文并列成分按顺序对应）
advancedExpressions.example: Tom and Mike scored 90 and 85 respectively. 汤姆和迈克分别得了90分和85分。

advancedExpressions.expression: make our respective contributions（做出我们各自的贡献（课文原句）） / their respective fields（他们各自的领域） / one's respective + 复数名词（各自的……（respective 只作定语，后接复数名词）） / their respective departments（他们各自的部门）
advancedExpressions.example: We all make our respective contributions. 我们都做出各自的贡献。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The two researchers returned to their respective laboratories, carrying separate sets of samples.

original_sentence: Moreover, there are people who choose to step out of their comfort zone and commit themselves to working for the benefit of others.
definitionEn: an area with a particular purpose, feature, condition, or official boundary

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （熟词僻义）把（土地）划作特定用途；分区规划
uncommonMeanings.example: This land is zoned for industrial use. 这块地被规划为工业用地。

posExamples.sentence: The school created a quiet zone beside the library.
Rescuers entered the danger zone only after the gas leak stopped.
Farmers in this climate zone grow olives and grapes.

wordForms.noun: zone 区域（因特定用途或特征划出）
wordForms.other: 拼读注意：zone /zəʊn/ 与 phone 押韵；短语动词 zone out（美，口语）走神：I zoned out during the lecture. 我听课走神了。

idioms.translation: （口语）处于最佳状态，进入化境
idioms.example: The player was in the zone and couldn't miss. 那名球员状态神勇，弹无虚发。

collocations.phrase: step out of their comfort zone
collocations.example: They choose to step out of their comfort zone. 他们选择走出舒适区。
London and Beijing are in different time zones. 伦敦和北京在不同时区。
Shenzhen was China's first special economic zone. 深圳是中国第一个经济特区。
Reporters risked their lives in the war zone. 记者们在战区冒着生命危险。
You can't leave your car in a no-parking zone. 禁停区不能停车。
The rear carriage is designated as a quiet zone.
Police moved spectators away from the danger zone.
This tree cannot survive outside its natural climate zone.

synonyms.example: This is a mountainous area. 这是山区。
synonyms.usage: area 最通用，泛指任何一片地方；zone 指因特定用途、功能或特征而'划定'的区域（time/danger/economic zone），带有'人为划界'意味。

synonyms.example: The Arctic region is warming fast. 北极地区正迅速变暖。
synonyms.usage: region 指较大的地理或行政区域（沿海地区、自治区）；zone 通常范围较小且功能性强。两者都作可数名词。

synonyms.example: She lives in the business district. 她住在商业区。
synonyms.usage: district 侧重城市或国家内正式划分的行政区（Haidian District）；zone 侧重功能划分而非行政划分。

advancedExpressions.expression: comfort zone 舒适区 / time zone 时区 / economic zone 经济区 / danger zone 危险地带 / war zone 战区 / earthquake zone 地震带 / no-smoking zone 禁烟区
advancedExpressions.example: zone 前加名词或形容词构成'……区'，高考阅读高频。

advancedExpressions.expression: area（泛指）→ region（大区域）→ district（行政区）→ zone（功能区）→ belt（带状区：the wheat belt 小麦产区）
advancedExpressions.example: 按'泛—大—行政—功能—带状'排序记忆。

advancedExpressions.expression: step out of their comfort zone（走出舒适区（课文原句）） / a time zone（时区） / an economic zone（经济区） / a danger/war zone（危险地带／战区）
advancedExpressions.example: They choose to step out of their comfort zone. 他们选择走出舒适区。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The school created a quiet zone beside the library.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The school created a quiet zone beside the library, giving students a place for silent study.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Rescuers entered the danger zone only after the gas leak stopped.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Rescuers entered the danger zone only after the gas leak stopped, wearing protective masks and carrying detectors.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

classPractice.question: 用 zone / area / district 填空：Because of the eight-hour time difference, they are in different time ____s.
classPractice.note: time zone 时区，固定搭配。

classPractice.question: 只有走出舒适区，你才能真正成长。Only by stepping out of your ____ ____ can you truly grow.
classPractice.note: 呼应课文词块；only + 状语置于句首时主句部分倒装。

classPractice.question: The coastal areas were declared a special economic ____ in the 1980s.
classPractice.note: special economic zone 经济特区。

original_sentence: Moreover, there are people who choose to step out of their comfort zone and commit themselves to working for the benefit of others.
definitionEn: a situation in which someone feels familiar, secure, and free from challenge

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 安慰；令人安慰的人或事物（a comfort to sb）
uncommonMeanings.example: Her children are a great comfort to her. 孩子们是她极大的安慰。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 安慰，抚慰
uncommonMeanings.example: She comforted the crying child. 她安慰哭泣的孩子。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 舒适，安逸（in comfort 舒适地）
uncommonMeanings.example: They live in comfort. 他们生活安逸。

posExamples.sentence: Speaking at the conference pushed Lina beyond her comfort zone.
The coach encourages athletes to step outside their comfort zone.
Routine tasks kept him safely inside his comfort zone.

wordForms.noun: comfort 舒适；安慰
wordForms.adjective: comfortable 舒适的；comforting 令人宽慰的
wordForms.other: comfort zone 复合名词，重音在 comfort 上；注意所有格搭配：one's comfort zone（out of my/your/their comfort zone）。

collocations.phrase: step out of one's comfort zone
collocations.example: There are people who choose to step out of their comfort zone. 有些人选择走出舒适区。

collocations.phrase: move/get out of one's comfort zone
collocations.example: Learning a language forces you to get out of your comfort zone. 学语言迫使你离开舒适区。
If you always stay in your comfort zone, you'll never improve. 总待在舒适区就永远不会进步。

collocations.phrase: push sb out of their comfort zone
collocations.example: A good coach pushes you out of your comfort zone. 好教练会把你推出舒适区。
Leading the debate took Marcus beyond his comfort zone.
Try to step outside your comfort zone once a week.
She knew that staying inside her comfort zone would limit her growth.
Small daily challenges can gradually expand your comfort zone.

synonyms.example: Home is her safe space. 家是她的安全地带。
synonyms.usage: safe space 侧重'免受伤害、可放心表达'的环境；comfort zone 是心理学比喻，指'熟悉、无压力但也无成长'的状态，常与 step out of 连用表挑战自我。

synonyms.example: Technical interviews are familiar territory for her.
synonyms.usage: familiar territory 作表语或名词短语，强调熟悉；comfort zone 常与 stay in、step outside、push beyond 搭配，强调心理安全感。

advancedExpressions.expression: step out of one's comfort zone 走出舒适区 / challenge oneself 挑战自我 / push one's limits 突破极限 / venture into the unknown 探索未知 / take on new challenges 迎接新挑战
advancedExpressions.example: 写作'成长/奋斗'话题的高分替换表达。

advancedExpressions.expression: There are people who choose to do A and commit themselves to doing B（有些人选择做A并致力于做B）
advancedExpressions.example: There are people who choose to step out of their comfort zone and commit themselves to working for the benefit of others.（注意 commit oneself to 中 to 是介词，后接 doing）

advancedExpressions.expression: step out of one's comfort zone（走出舒适区（课文原句）） / move/get out of one's comfort zone（离开舒适区） / stay in/within one's comfort zone（待在舒适区） / push sb out of their comfort zone（把某人推出舒适区）
advancedExpressions.example: There are people who choose to step out of their comfort zone. 有些人选择走出舒适区。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Speaking at the conference pushed Lina beyond her comfort zone.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Speaking at the conference pushed Lina beyond her comfort zone, yet she answered every question with growing confidence.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The coach encourages athletes to step outside their comfort zone.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The coach encourages athletes to step outside their comfort zone, introducing one demanding drill at a time.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

classPractice.question: 此外，有些人选择走出舒适区，致力于为他人谋福利。Moreover, there are people who choose to ____ ____ ____ their comfort zone and commit themselves to ____ (work) for the benefit of others.
classPractice.note: 课文原句；commit oneself to 的 to 是介词，接 doing。

classPractice.question: 学习一门新技能意味着走出你的舒适区。
classPractice.answer: Learning a new skill means stepping out of your comfort zone.
classPractice.note: mean doing sth 意味着做某事；mean to do 打算做。

classPractice.question: Only when you leave your comfort zone ____ (do) real growth begin.
classPractice.note: only + 状语从句置于句首，主句部分倒装。

translation: vt. & vi. vt. 操作，使运行 vi. 运转，工作；经营，营业
definitionEn: (1) to control or use a machine (2) to function or conduct business (3) to perform surgery

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 动手术（operate on sb for sth 给某人做……手术）
uncommonMeanings.example: Surgeons operated on Max for a brain aneurysm. 外科医生为马克斯做了脑动脉瘤手术。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （公司、组织在某地）经营，运营
uncommonMeanings.example: The airline operates in more than 20 countries. 这家航空公司在20多个国家运营。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （熟词僻义）企业，公司（课件例句）
uncommonMeanings.example: The two parent groups now run their business as a single combined operation. 两家母公司现在把业务合并为一家企业经营。

posExamples.sentence: Only trained staff may operate the laser cutter.
The ferry operates between the islands throughout winter.
Surgeons operated on the injured climber that evening.

wordForms.noun: operation 手术；运转；实施；（军事）行动；企业。operator 操作员；接线员；经营者
wordForms.verb: operate 操作；运转；动手术；经营。cooperate 合作（co- '共同' + operate）
wordForms.adjective: operative 生效的，实施中的（become operative 生效）；operational 运转中的，可使用的
wordForms.other: 重音在第一音节 /ˈɒpəreɪt/；operation 重音后移到 -ra- /ˌɒpəˈreɪʃn/。记忆链：operate → operation → operator → operative。

collocations.example: Only trained workers may operate the machinery. 只有受过培训的工人才能操作机器。
The bus is designed to operate in all weather conditions. 这种公交车可在各种天气下运行。
Surgeons operated on Max for a brain aneurysm. 外科医生为马克斯做了脑动脉瘤手术。
It's time to put our plan into operation. 是时候实施我们的计划了。
The new rules come into operation on January 1. 新规1月1日生效。
The system has been in operation for six months. 该系统已运行六个月。
He had an operation on his lung. 他做了肺部手术。
The doctor performed an operation to remove the tumor. 医生做手术切除了肿瘤。
The soldiers were engaged in a military operation close to the border. 士兵们在边境附近执行军事行动。
The law becomes operative next month. 该法律下月生效。

synonyms.example: She runs a small restaurant. 她经营一家小餐馆。
synonyms.usage: 表'经营'时 run 更口语、operate 更正式，都可接 a business/company；表'机器运转'时二者都可作不及物动词：The machine runs/operates smoothly。但'动手术'只能用 operate on。

synonyms.example: The elevator isn't working. 电梯坏了。
synonyms.usage: work 指机器'能正常工作/没坏'，也指药物、办法'起作用'；operate 侧重'处于运行状态'且更正式，还可带宾语表'操作'（operate the machinery），work 表'操作'时说 work a machine 较少见。

synonyms.example: He manages a hotel. 他管理一家酒店。
synonyms.usage: manage 强调'管理人和事务'；operate 强调'使机构/设备运转'。manage 还有 manage to do（设法做成）的用法，operate 没有。

advancedExpressions.expression: put ... into operation 实施 / come into operation 生效 / in operation 生效中，运转中 / have an operation 接受手术 / do/perform/carry out an operation 做手术 / a military operation 军事行动 / a combined operation 联合企业
advancedExpressions.example: The soldiers were engaged in a military operation close to the Ugandan border.（课件例句）

advancedExpressions.expression: operate + -ion → operation；+ -or 表'人/物' → operator；+ -ive → operative；co- + operate → cooperate 合作 → cooperation 合作
advancedExpressions.example: -or 表'人'类比：operator, visitor, editor, inventor。

advancedExpressions.expression: come into operation = come into effect/force = become operative = take effect（新规、法律'生效'）
advancedExpressions.example: The new rules come into operation / take effect on January 1.

sentenceUpgrade.original: Only trained staff may operate the laser cutter.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Only trained staff may operate the laser cutter, following a checklist before activating the machine.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The ferry operates between the islands throughout winter, carrying food and medical supplies despite rough seas.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

classPractice.question: 外科医生为 Max 做了脑动脉瘤手术。____ ____ ____ Max ____ a brain aneurysm (动脉瘤).
classPractice.note: operate on sb for sth 给某人做……的手术；operate 表'动手术'是不及物动词，必须接 on。

classPractice.question: She had an ____ (operate) on her lung to remove a tumor.
classPractice.note: have an operation on + 部位 接受……部位的手术。

classPractice.note: in operation 生效中、运转中，与延续性的完成时连用。

classPractice.question: You need a licence to ____ (operation) this crane.
classPractice.note: to 后接动词原形；operate 及物用法'操作（机器）'。

translation: vt. & vi. & n. vt. & vi. 聘用，雇用；租用 n. 新雇员；租借
original_sentence: However, in the future, employers will look to hire people who are ready and able to learn.
definitionEn: (1) to employ someone (2) to pay to use something temporarily (3) the act or cost of hiring

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 租用，租借（常用于 for hire / on hire）
uncommonMeanings.example: Bicycles are available for hire at the park gate. 公园门口有自行车出租。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 新雇员（a new hire）
uncommonMeanings.example: All new hires receive two weeks of training. 所有新员工都要接受两周培训。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （英）短期租用（物）；（美）雇用（人）
uncommonMeanings.example: We hired a boat by the hour. 我们按小时租了一条船。

posExamples.sentence: The gallery hired two guides for the summer exhibition.
We hired a van to transport the stage equipment.
Bicycles are available for hire near the station.

wordForms.noun: hire（租用；新雇员）；hirer 租用人
wordForms.other: 英美差异贴士：英式 hire＝短期租物/雇人，rent＝长期租房；美式租车、租房都常用 rent，雇人用 hire。房屋招租：美 for rent，英 to let。

idioms.example: The taxi had its 'For Hire' sign lit. 那辆出租车亮着'空车'牌。

collocations.translation: 指望聘用……的人（课文原句）
collocations.example: Employers will look to hire people who are ready and able to learn. 雇主会指望聘用乐于并善于学习的人。

collocations.translation: 【课件】租一辆车（英式，短期租用）
collocations.example: We hired a car for the weekend. 我们租了辆车过周末。
The shop hires out bikes and cars. 这家店出租自行车和汽车。

collocations.phrase: hire a lawyer to handle the case
collocations.example: They hired a lawyer to handle the case. 他们聘请了一位律师处理这个案子。
Boats are for hire on the lake. 湖上有船出租。
I rented a car from him for a month. 我向他租了一个月的车。
She rents out her spare room to a student. 她把空余的房间租给一名学生。

collocations.translation: 【课件】（房屋等）供出租（美式 for rent，英式 to let）
collocations.example: There is a sign saying 'To Let' outside the house. 房子外面挂着'此房出租'的牌子。

synonyms.example: The firm employs over 500 people worldwide. 这家公司在全球雇用五百多人。
synonyms.usage: employ 指长期、正式雇用，宾语是人，常用被动 be employed as/in；hire 可指短期雇用或（英）租物；不说 employ a car。

synonyms.example: They rent a flat near the office. 他们在办公室附近租了套公寓。
synonyms.usage: 方向靠介词区分：rent sth from sb 租入，rent sth (out) to sb 租出；英式租房用 rent、短期租物用 hire；hire out＝租出。

synonyms.example: She lets the cottage to tourists in summer. 夏天她把小屋租给游客。
synonyms.usage: let 只用于房主把房出租（let sth to sb），不能表示'租入'；招牌语 to let＝待租。

advancedExpressions.expression: hire a car 租入 / hire out a car 租出 / be for hire 供租用 / hire a lawyer 聘请律师 / rent sth from sb 租入 / rent (out) sth to sb 租出 / for rent · to let 房屋招租
advancedExpressions.example: The hall is for hire; you can also rent equipment from the manager. 大厅可供租用，你还可以向经理租设备。

advancedExpressions.expression: hire sb / employ sb / take on sb / recruit sb 招聘
advancedExpressions.example: The company is taking on extra staff for the summer. 公司正在增聘暑期员工。

collocations.phrase: soft skills such as communication, cooperation and leadership
collocations.translation: 沟通、合作、领导力等软技能（课文原句）
collocations.example: Employees will need to demonstrate excellent soft skills such as leadership. 雇员需要展现出色的软技能，如领导力。
The course helps students develop leadership skills. 这门课帮助学生培养领导才能。

The museum reopened under new leadership last spring.

synonyms.example: He completed the project under his tutor's guidance. 他在导师指导下完成了项目。
synonyms.usage: guidance 指给出建议、方向的'指导'，常搭配 under sb's guidance；leadership 强调统率、带领团队的能力与地位，常搭配 under the leadership of。

synonyms.example: The choir sang under the direction of Mr Hall. 合唱团在霍尔先生指挥下演唱。

original_sentence: You may have a brilliant idea, but before you decide to put it into action, it is wise to weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of this option.
definitionEn: to consider and compare the facts, advantages, and disadvantages before deciding

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 重达（连系动词用法，无被动、无进行时）
uncommonMeanings.example: The baby weighs four kilos. 婴儿重四公斤。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 称……的重量
uncommonMeanings.example: She weighed the parcel before posting it. 寄包裹前她先称了重。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 权衡，斟酌，仔细考虑
uncommonMeanings.example: He weighed up his chances of success. 他掂量了自己成功的可能性。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 使忧虑，成为心头负担
uncommonMeanings.example: The debt weighed on her for years. 债务让她忧心多年。

posExamples.sentence: Nora weighed up the job offer before moving abroad.
The panel must weigh up the evidence from both experts.
Weigh up the risks before investing your savings.

wordForms.noun: weight 重量；重担（lose/put on weight 减肥/增重）
wordForms.verb: weigh 称重；重达；权衡；outweigh 超过，比……重要
wordForms.adjective: weighty 沉重的；重要的；overweight 超重的
wordForms.other: 拼写贴士：weigh 与 eight、neighbour 同含 -eigh，gh 不发音，读 /weɪ/；名词 weight 加 t。表'重达'时 weigh 不用被动语态。

idioms.example: Passing the exam was a weight off my mind. 考试通过让我如释重负。
His opinion carries a lot of weight with the boss. 他的意见在老板那里很有分量。
Everyone in the team must pull their weight. 团队每个人都必须尽本分。

collocations.phrase: weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of
collocations.example: It is wise to weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of this option. 明智的是权衡这个选择的利弊。
I weighed the benefits of the plan against the risks involved. 我认真权衡了计划的优点和有关的风险。
She spoke slowly, weighing what she would say. 她说得很慢，斟酌着措辞。
The fear of failure weighed heavily on his mind. 对失败的害怕沉重地压在他心上。

collocations.translation: 【课件】心头重负的解除，如释重负
collocations.example: The news was certainly a weight off my mind. 这消息真让我如释重负。
Weigh the pros and cons before you decide. 决定前先权衡利弊。
Councillors will weigh up the proposal at Tuesday's meeting.
Researchers weighed up competing evidence before publishing.

synonyms.example: We are considering moving to the city. 我们正考虑搬到城里。
synonyms.usage: consider 泛指'考虑'，接 doing/名词/从句；weigh (up) 强调把利弊两面放在'天平'上比较，常接 the advantages and disadvantages、A against B、疑问词从句。

synonyms.example: Experts assessed the damage after the storm. 专家评估了风暴后的损失。
synonyms.usage: assess/evaluate 是较正式的'评定价值/程度'，宾语常为 situation, damage, performance；weigh up 口语化，突出取舍前的反复掂量。

synonyms.example: You must balance work against family life. 你必须在工作和家庭间求得平衡。
synonyms.usage: balance A against B 与 weigh A against B 结构相同，balance 更强调'兼顾两边'，weigh 更强调'比出轻重再决定'。

advancedExpressions.type: 语法点·名词性从句（课件）

advancedExpressions.example: Before acting, weigh up whether the benefits outweigh the risks. 行动前先权衡收益是否大于风险。

advancedExpressions.expression: weigh up 权衡 / weigh A against B 比较 / weigh on sb 使忧虑 / weigh in (with) 发表意见 / outweigh 超过
advancedExpressions.example: The advantages far outweigh the disadvantages. 优点远大于缺点。

advancedExpressions.expression: weigh up the pros and cons / weigh the benefits against the risks / think over / take...into consideration
advancedExpressions.example: Take all the factors into consideration before you choose a career. 择业前把所有因素考虑进去。

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

classPractice.answer: Before you decide to put it into action, it is wise to weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of this option.
classPractice.note: weigh up the advantages and disadvantages of...；put...into action 付诸行动。

translation: n. 收到的款项，收入；收据
definitionEn: (1) a written or electronic record that payment was made (2) the act of receiving something

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 收据，小票
uncommonMeanings.example: Always check your receipt before leaving the shop. 离店前一定核对小票。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 收到，接到（正式；on/in receipt of）

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 收到的款项，进款，收入
uncommonMeanings.example: Box-office receipts rose by 20% last year. 去年票房收入增长了20%。

posExamples.sentence: Please keep the receipt until the warranty expires.

wordForms.adjective: receptive 乐于接受（新思想）的
wordForms.other: 发音贴士：receipt 中的 p 不发音，读 /rɪˈsiːt/（类似 debt 的 b、island 的 s 不发音）。形近词：receipt 收据 ≠ recipe /ˈresəpi/ 食谱、秘诀。

collocations.example: Johnston was in receipt of state benefits. 约翰斯顿正在领取政府救济金。
Keep the receipt in case you want to return the goods. 保留收据以防退货。
The office acknowledged receipt of my application that afternoon.
Please request proof of receipt for the registered letter.
The machine automatically issues a receipt after payment.

synonyms.example: The company sent an invoice for the repairs. 公司寄来了维修费发票。
synonyms.usage: invoice 是付款前开出的'账单/发票'，要求对方付款；receipt 是付款后开具的'收据'，证明已付款。

synonyms.example: Could we have the bill, please? 请给我们结账好吗？

advancedExpressions.example: On receipt of your payment, we will ship the order. 一收到付款我们就发货。

advancedExpressions.expression: receipt /rɪˈsiːt/ 收据 · recipe /ˈresəpi/ 食谱 · recipient 接受者
advancedExpressions.example: She followed a recipe and kept the receipt for the ingredients. 她照着食谱做菜，还留着买食材的收据。

classPractice.note: on receipt of 一收到……（就）；比较 in receipt of（正在）领取着。

translation: adj. 商业的，贸易的；盈利的；商业性的
original_sentence: Another advantage is that you will be able to better provide for yourself and your family, or even the economy will benefit if you achieve commercial success.
definitionEn: related to business or profit-making, or intended to attract a large market

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 商业的，贸易的

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 以盈利为目的的；（常贬）商业化的
uncommonMeanings.example: Their music has become too commercial. 他们的音乐变得太商业化了。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （电视、广播中的）广告（熟词僻义）
uncommonMeanings.example: The TV commercial lasted thirty seconds. 那条电视广告长三十秒。

posExamples.sentence: The invention has considerable commercial potential.

wordForms.adjective: commercial 商业的
wordForms.other: 构词法：commerce + -ial → commercial；e-commerce 电子商务。重音：commercial /kəˈmɜːʃl/ 在第二音节。

collocations.translation: 取得商业成功（课文原句）

synonyms.example: The country faces serious economic problems. 该国面临严重的经济问题。
synonyms.usage: economic 修饰宏观'经济'（growth, crisis, policy）；commercial 修饰'商业、买卖、盈利'（success, value, bank）；economical 则是'节约的'。

advancedExpressions.expression: commerce 商业 → commercial 商业的；(电视)广告 → commercialize 使商业化 → commercially 商业上
advancedExpressions.example: The technology has not yet been commercialized. 这项技术尚未商业化。

advancedExpressions.expression: advertisement 广告(通用) / commercial 电视广播广告 / ad 口语 / poster 海报 / flyer 传单

advancedExpressions.example: Whether the film achieves commercial success depends on word of mouth. 影片能否获得商业成功取决于口碑。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The invention has considerable commercial potential.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The invention has considerable commercial potential, attracting interest from three manufacturers.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

sentenceUpgrade.original: The station earns most of its income from commercial advertising.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: The station earns most of its income from commercial advertising, broadcasting short promotions between programmes.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

classPractice.question: The invention has great ____ (commerce) value and will soon be put into production.

original_sentence: Towards the end of the interview, don’t forget to seize the moment and ask questions.
definitionEn: to take hold of something suddenly or by force, take control, or use an opportunity eagerly

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 抓住，把握（机会、时机）
uncommonMeanings.example: She seized the chance to study abroad. 她抓住了出国学习的机会。

uncommonMeanings.example: He seized my hand and shook it warmly. 他一把握住我的手热情地摇了摇。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 夺取，攻占（政权、阵地）
uncommonMeanings.example: The enemy seized the town at dawn. 敌军在拂晓时攻占了该镇。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: 没收；查获；（警方）抓捕
uncommonMeanings.example: Customs officers seized 100 kilos of smuggled goods. 海关官员查获了100公斤走私货物。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （熟词僻义）（情绪、疼痛）突然侵袭，攫住（常用被动 be seized by/with）
uncommonMeanings.example: He was seized by a sudden desire to laugh. 他突然很想笑。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: seize on/upon sth（急切地）利用，抓住（可用的事物）
uncommonMeanings.example: Reporters seized on his careless remark. 记者们立刻抓住他那句不慎的话大做文章。

uncommonMeanings.meaning: seize up（机器）卡住，失灵；（身体部位）僵住
uncommonMeanings.example: The engine seized up on the way home. 回家路上发动机卡死了。

posExamples.sentence: Police seized counterfeit goods at the border.

wordForms.noun: seizure（夺取；查获，没收；[疾病]突然发作）
wordForms.other: 拼写贴士：seize 是 "i before e except after c" 规则的例外词（同类还有 weird, either），是 ei 不是 ie；发音 /siːz/，注意与 cease /siːs/ 区分。

idioms.example: Seize the day, for life is short. 人生苦短，把握今天。

collocations.example: Don't forget to seize the moment and ask questions. 别忘了抓住时机提问。

collocations.example: His mother seized him by the arm. 他妈妈一把抓住他的胳膊。

collocations.example: Our army soon seized control of the city again. 我军很快重新夺回了这座城市的控制权。
He seized the gun from the bank robber. 他从银行劫匪手中夺过了枪。
The police seized three men for possession of illegal drugs. 警方因非法藏毒抓捕了三名男子。

collocations.translation: 【课件】被恐惧／惊慌攫住；突然感到害怕／惊慌
collocations.example: Panic seized her. 她惊慌失措。

collocations.translation: 【课件】正要做……这时……（when 引导并列分句）
collocations.example: The boy was about to run across the road when his mother seized him. 男孩正要跑过马路，这时妈妈一把抓住了他。

synonyms.example: She grasped the rope tightly. 她紧紧抓住绳子。
synonyms.usage: grasp 强调抓牢、握紧，也表"理解"（grasp the meaning）；seize 强调动作突然、用力，还可表"夺取/没收"，grasp 无此义。两者都可接 the opportunity。

synonyms.example: He grabbed his coat and ran out. 他一把抓起外套跑了出去。
synonyms.usage: grab 口语化，强调动作匆忙随意（grab a bite 匆匆吃点东西）；seize 更正式，强调果断有力。二者都可作及物动词直接带宾语。

synonyms.example: The thief snatched her bag and fled. 小偷抢了她的包就逃。
synonyms.usage: snatch 强调快速抢夺、常含"抢走不属于自己东西"之意（snatch sth from sb）；seize sth from sb 侧重用力夺取，未必非法。

advancedExpressions.example: The machine seized up, and panic seized the workers. 机器卡死了，工人们一阵惊慌。

advancedExpressions.expression: seize/grasp/take/jump at the opportunity to do sth；make the most of the chance
advancedExpressions.example: She jumped at the opportunity to work in the corporate world. 她欣然抓住进入企业界工作的机会。

original_sentence: For example, “Japanese was a minor subject I took and I know that expanding into Japan is part of your corporate plan.

advancedExpressions.example: Bowling is a sport that people of all ages can enjoy. 保龄球是老少皆宜的运动。

sentenceUpgrade.original: Our team goes bowling every Friday evening.
sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Our team goes bowling every Friday evening, keeping a friendly record of everyone's scores.
sentenceUpgrade.techniques: 保留原句主语、核心事实和场景，用补充成分具体说明方式、条件或结果。

sentenceUpgrade.upgraded: Fast bowling troubled the opening batters, forcing them to defend rather than attack.

classPractice.question: I often go ____ (bowl) with my friends at weekends to relax myself.
classPractice.note: go + V-ing 表"去做某项运动/休闲活动"，固定用动名词形式。

classPractice.question: 我们都被这个意外的消息惊呆了。We were all ____ ____ by the unexpected news.
classPractice.note: bowl sb over 使大为惊讶，常用被动语态 be bowled over by。

classPractice.question: 我还为几场本地体育赛事做过临时工作，比如保龄球锦标赛。（temporary, like）
classPractice.answer: I also did some temporary work for several local sporting events, like the bowling tournament.
classPractice.note: 课文原句回译；like 在此表举例，相当于 such as。

original_sentence: I also did some temporary work for several local sporting events, like the bowling tournament.
definitionEn: a competition in which many players or teams take part through a series of games or matches

uncommonMeanings.meaning: （中世纪骑士的）马上比武大会（历史义，词的本源）
uncommonMeanings.example: Knights showed their skills at tournaments in the Middle Ages. 中世纪骑士在比武大会上展示技艺。

posExamples.sentence: Sixteen schools entered the regional chess tournament.
The tennis tournament was postponed by heavy rain.
She reached the tournament final without losing a set.

wordForms.noun: tournament 锦标赛（可数名词，复数 tournaments）
wordForms.other: 词源：tourn- 意为"转"（同源词 turn, tour），原指骑士骑马回转交锋的比武，后引申为多轮赛制的锦标赛；发音有两读 /ˈtʊənəmənt/ 或 /ˈtɔːnəmənt/，重音都在第一音节

collocations.translation: 保龄球锦标赛（课文原句）
collocations.example: I did some temporary work for local sporting events, like the bowling tournament. 我为本地体育赛事做过临时工作，比如保龄球锦标赛。

collocations.translation: 网球/国际象棋/高尔夫锦标赛（tournament 前常加项目名）
collocations.example: She won her first tennis tournament at the age of 15. 她15岁赢得了首个网球锦标赛冠军。
Our city will host an international chess tournament next year. 我们市明年将举办国际象棋锦标赛。

collocations.phrase: enter / take part in / compete in a tournament
collocations.example: More than 100 players entered the tournament. 一百多名选手参加了这次锦标赛。
The young team surprised everyone by winning the tournament. 这支年轻的队伍赢得锦标赛，令所有人惊讶。
In a knockout tournament, one defeat means the end. 在淘汰赛中，输一场就意味着出局。
Only the top eight teams qualify for the final tournament. 只有前八名的队伍能获得决赛阶段参赛资格。
Four junior teams entered the tournament this year.

synonyms.example: We watched a football match between the two schools. 我们看了两校之间的一场足球赛。
synonyms.usage: match（英式）指球类等的"单场"比赛；tournament 指多场次、多轮赛制的"整个赛事"，一个 tournament 由许多 matches 组成。

synonyms.example: She took first prize in the English speech competition. 她在英语演讲比赛中获得一等奖。
synonyms.usage: competition 最泛用，可指比赛也可指抽象的"竞争"（不可数）；tournament 专指体育、棋牌类的锦标赛，语义更窄。

synonyms.example: He entered a photography contest and won. 他参加摄影比赛并获了奖。
synonyms.usage: contest 多指由评委打分评出优胜者的比赛（演讲、歌唱、摄影等）；tournament 靠对阵胜负、多轮淘汰或积分决出名次。

synonyms.example: The World Table Tennis Championships are held every two years. 世乒赛每两年举行一次。
synonyms.usage: championship 强调"决出冠军（champion）"的最高级别赛事，赛事名中常用复数（the World Championships）；tournament 不强调级别，任何多轮赛制比赛都可用。

advancedExpressions.expression: match 单场球赛（英）/ game 一场比赛（美）/ race 速度赛 / contest 评比赛 / competition 泛指比赛与竞争 / tournament 多轮锦标赛 / championship 冠军赛
advancedExpressions.example: He lost the first match but still won the tournament. 他首场比赛失利，但仍赢得了整个锦标赛。

advancedExpressions.expression: enter / compete in a tournament 参赛；beat / defeat sb 击败某人（宾语是人）；win a match / prize 赢得比赛/奖项（宾语是物）
advancedExpressions.example: They beat the host team and won the tournament. 他们击败东道主队，赢得了锦标赛。

advancedExpressions.expression: tournament（骑士回转交锋→锦标赛）、tour（转一圈→旅行）、turn（转动）同源
advancedExpressions.example: The word tournament comes from knights turning to fight. tournament 一词源于骑士回转交锋。

classPractice.question:
用 match / tournament / contest / race 的适当形式填空：
1) Liu Xiang won the 110m hurdles ____ in Athens.
2) Thirty-two teams will take part in the World Cup ____.
3) Our class won the football ____ against Class 2 yesterday.
4) She came first in the school speech ____.
classPractice.note: race 速度赛；tournament 多轮赛制的整个赛事；match 单场球赛；contest 评委评比类竞赛。

classPractice.question: Only the top four players will qualify ____ the national chess tournament.
classPractice.note: qualify for... 获得……的资格；参加锦标赛还可说 enter / take part in / compete in a tournament。

classPractice.question: 这位16岁的选手在国际网球锦标赛中获得冠军。The 16-year-old player won the championship in the international tennis ____.
classPractice.note: tournament 指整个赛事，championship 在此指"冠军（头衔）"，注意二者搭配区别。
